gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a power station used as sump-pump backup has to have its AC-ECO auto-off disabled. BLUETTI's manual says AC-ECO ships enabled and turns the AC off when output stays below a set level for a set time. An idle sump pump draws 0 W between cycles, so during an outage the outlet can be dead when the float rises. BLUETTI's 'Lifting Power' figure is a resistive-load mode, so it is not headroom for starting a motor.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited Consumer Reports pages (buying guide, buying guide duplicate, best backup systems) and SEC America's selection guide. CR sizes only 12 V deep-cycle batteries: 75–120 Ah, about 7–8 h of active pumping, tested with a 75 Ah AGM at 10 ft lift. CR publishes no amp, watt, surge, inverter or power-station figures. SEC America gives no sizing figures at all. ChatGPT's own answer lists 'inverter + battery' with no setup caveat. None of them mention auto-off, UPS behavior or motor-start limits. I rate this 2, not 3: the 'ECO on by default' text is from BLUETTI's sibling AC200P L manual, because the Elite 100 V2 manual PDF would not render as text for me.
kit_items: Battery and inverter for the existing 120 V AC primary pump: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2. It has 1,024 Wh of LiFePO4 and 1,800 W of continuous AC. It switches to battery in ≤10 ms (UPS), so it can sit plugged in between the wall and the pump. It refills 80% in 45 min on 1,200 W AC. After setup, turn AC-ECO off in the app or with the buttons.

Setting, not a product: power the pump from the power station's AC outlet and confirm AC-ECO is off. Size by the pump's nameplate amps: runtime h ≈ 1,024 Wh ÷ (nameplate A × 120 V × fraction of time the pump runs). I could not source a typical pump's amps or start surge, so check the nameplate rather than BLUETTI's 2,700 W 'Lifting Power' figure.

findings.label: Battery capacity and chemistry
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: Maker's US product page. For comparison, CR's test battery holds 12 V × 75 Ah = 900 Wh nominal, so 1,024 Wh ÷ 900 Wh ≈ 1.14× that battery's nominal energy.

findings.label: AC output
findings.value: 1,800 W continuous, 120 V, 15 A; '2,700 W Lifting Power'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: The page gives no separate surge or peak figure for motors. 'Lifting Power' is BLUETTI's resistive-load mode (see the AC200P L manual finding), so it does not show that a pump motor can start.

findings.label: UPS switchover time
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: Maker's claim: 'Switches to battery power in just 10 ms'. This lets the unit stay inline between the wall outlet and the pump.

findings.label: AC refill time
findings.value: 80% in 45 min at 1,200 W AC input
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: 0.8 × 1,024 Wh = 819 Wh in 0.75 h, about 1,092 W average into the battery. When the grid returns between storms, it is mostly refilled in under an hour.

findings.label: Price, maker's US store
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | 1,800W 1,024Wh
findings.note: storecheck.py product: variant 'Elite 100 V2', price 499.0, available true.

findings.product: BLUETTI AC200P L (sibling model, same maker)
findings.label: AC-ECO default and behavior
findings.value: AC-ECO and DC-ECO enabled by default; AC turns off when output stays below a set level for a set time; AC-ECO unavailable while charging from AC
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC200P L User Manual, section 9.5 ECO Mode (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Manual quote: 'The AC-ECO and DC-ECO modes are enabled by default to save energy.' Implication: while the grid is up, ECO is inactive. Once the grid fails, an idle pump (0 W between cycles) can trigger the shut-off. This is the AC200P L manual, not the Elite 100 V2 manual. The Elite 100 V2 manual lists a '5.4 ECO Mode' section, but its PDF would not render as text for me.

findings.product: BLUETTI AC200P L (sibling model, same maker)
findings.label: Power Lifting Mode scope
findings.value: Resistive loads only, 2,400–3,600 W; actual operating power stays at 2,400 W
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC200P L User Manual, section 9.4 Power Lifting Mode (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Examples given are kettles, hair dryers and electric blankets. So a 'Lifting Power' figure does not count toward starting a pump motor.

findings.label: Battery sizing the cited rival gives
findings.value: 75–120 Ah 12 V deep-cycle; 7–8 h of active pumping per full charge; CR test battery 75 Ah AGM at 10 ft lift
findings.source_title: Sump Pump Backup System Buying Guide - Consumer Reports
findings.note: This is the rival baseline. It gives no amps, watts, surge, inverter or power-station figures.

unsourced: Running amps and start (locked-rotor) current of a typical 1/3 HP and 1/2 HP primary pump (Zoeller M53, Wayne CDU790/CDU800). zoellerpumps.com returned 404; the Ferguson, SupplyHouse, Pollard and USABlueBook pages returned 403; the Wayne manual PDF would not render; the ManualsHive copy failed TLS. So the runtime arithmetic stays a formula built on the pump's nameplate amps.

Elite 100 V2 motor surge or peak watts. The product page lists only 1,800 W rated and 2,700 W 'Lifting Power'. The support page and manual PDF (s4.bluettipower.com/...0f613cd7.pdf) did not render as text.

Elite 100 V2's own AC-ECO default, low-load threshold and timeout. The manual lists a section '5.4 ECO Mode', but I could not read it. Forum threads describing a 4-hour timeout redirect to forum.bluettipower.com, so I could not open them.
Elite 100 V2 self-consumption (idle watts) with AC on and no load. Nothing opened gives a maker figure or a named measurement, so I can't say how many hours of standby the 1,024 Wh covers.
Duty cycle (fraction of time the pump runs) during heavy rain. None of the opened sources gives a figure.
